subject: Re: Aligning scope — convert intro demo into hands-on engineering sprint
messages:
From: Sam Evans <sam.evans@acme.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Intro demo request: Redwood inference overview

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks — we're ready to see Redwood next week. Right now the ask from our platform team is pretty specific: we want to evaluate end-to-end latency, routing behavior for multi-tenant workloads, and options for a private deployment. At first glance an intro demo would be fine, but given the technical depth we might prefer a deep-dive so the engineering leads can weigh in.

Can you propose 60–90 minute slots next week? Primary attendees from our side would be me, Priya Rao (platform eng), and our infra lead (TBD). We have travel the week of 24 May (company offsite), so earlier in the week is better.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Evans
Director, Integrations | ACME Corp
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Sam Evans <sam.evans@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro demo request: Redwood inference overview

Hi Sam — thanks for the context. Given the goals you listed (latency/routing/private deployment) I recommend converting the intro into a hands-on engineering sprint / technical deep-dive. That will let the platform and infra leads run sample requests, inspect traces, and discuss a realistic rollout plan.

Proposed format (90 minutes):
- 00–15m: quick product framing + success criteria
- 15–60m: live runbook + sample workload (we'll bring a test harness)
- 60–80m: deployment options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and SLA/compliance checklist
- 80–90m: next steps + action items (POC scope, data/security contacts)

Possible slots (PST):
- Tue, 25 May — 09:00–10:30 or 13:00–14:30
- Wed, 26 May — 11:00–12:30

If those don't work because of your offsite/travel, we can also target Mon, 24 May afternoon (shorter 60-minute slot).

Prep we need from your side:
- list of attendees + roles
- a short sample prompt/workload or token distribution (if you can share a redacted example)

I'll attach a 1‑page prework checklist and a lightweight architecture sample so your infra lead has context.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
Attachments: acme-prework-checklist.pdf, redwood-architecture-sample.json
From: Sam Evans <sam.evans@acme.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro demo request: Redwood inference overview

Thanks Soojin — the sprint format sounds perfect. Quick scheduling note: our infra lead is traveling Tue/Wed for customer work and won't be available until Thursday afternoon (PST). Priya and I are in the office Tues morning but then leave for the offsite midday.

Given that, our two workable windows are:
- Thu, 27 May 15:00–16:30 PST
- Fri, 28 May 09:00–10:30 PST

If neither works, we can do a 60-minute sync Wed 26 May 11:00–12:00 but without the infra lead.

Apologies for the late logistics — travel landed after we first talked.

Sam — locking Thu, 27 May 15:00–16:30 PST for the hands-on sprint.

I've created a calendar event and shared a short agenda + the prework doc (see link). Vivek will bring the runtime engineer to run the test harness; I'll coordinate the invites with your infra lead once you confirm their email.

Quick ask for your infra lead (if available): can you provision a small sample of traffic (curl examples or a JSON payload) and a short list of success metrics (p95 latency target, token budget) so we can tailor the test run?

Look forward to it — we'll send the calendar link and a HubSpot activity record HS-12345.
